title: Congregational Care
definition: Congregational Care is the shared ministry of watching over, comforting, encouraging, correcting, and helping one another in the body of Christ.
summary: Congregational Care is the shared responsibility of the church body to bear burdens, comfort, encourage, and help one another endure.
christFocus: Jesus Christ cares for His sheep and teaches His people to love one another as He has loved them.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Congregational care is the church's shared responsibility to watch over, encourage, and support its members. Scripture gives pastors a shepherding role, but it also calls the whole body to bear one another's burdens.

This care includes prayer, visitation, practical help, correction, encouragement, presence in suffering, and patient discipleship. It is ordinary love organized around real people.

Jesus cares for His sheep through His Word, His Spirit, and His people. Congregational care becomes one way His shepherding love is made visible.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because people can disappear spiritually while still being near the church. Congregational care helps the church notice the hurting, the drifting, the disabled, the recovering, and the overwhelmed before they are forgotten.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Learn names, notice absences, ask sincere questions, and follow up with action. Do not leave care only to leaders; become part of Christ's shepherding presence in the body.
